lines: P R O C E E D I N G S
HIS HONOUR:  Thank you.  Before we begin, can I just mention
two points.
First, to remind the parties that I would like
a copy of the chronology cross-referenced to the
bundles.
Also, I would like just a little help as to how the
bundles have been put together.  They are certainly not
in chronological order; what order are they in?
MR JONES:  It's a very good question, the sort of question
that I --
HIS HONOUR:  The rules require a chronological bundle, and
it is quite difficult thinking -- well, I would like to
see the {A2-3} and {A3-4} to which that document is an
answer, and then you have to, by pure chance, go about
four bundles further on, which slightly ... (Pause)
But they have just been divided up with tabs.
MR JONES:  I mean, one option is the parties assist you by
producing an agreed bundle -- hopefully when we have
done our written closings with reference in {A1-10} and
HIS HONOUR:  I would be grateful.  There was always a risk
anyway of seeing the document in two different places.
MR JONES:  We'll secure that for you.
Could I ask your Honour, please, to take up the list
of issues.  It can be found in {E2-34}.
In {B3-2}, there are two sets of lists of issues.
There's a case memorandum list of issues from the --
HIS HONOUR:  The parties weren't able to agree on the list
of issues?
MR JONES:  That's right, yes.  Slightly --
HIS HONOUR:  It's not unknown, Mr Jones.
MR JONES:  The bank and the first defendant were able to
agree on what they thought were the list of issues.
HIS HONOUR:  Of course.  That goes without saying.
MR JONES:  My learned friend took you to these yesterday in
relation to his submissions about the issue estoppel,
and made the point that the July 2003 dishonest
statement was not an issue.
I mean, that's absolutely right, because I'll
develop -- that's actually a point in our favour, but
perhaps, first of all, we could turn to {D2-12}.
HIS HONOUR:  Yes.
MR JONES:  This is within the claimant's list of issues,
just to see how narrowly focused the misrepresentation
issue in the 2001 trial was.
One can see that summarised at {A1-5}, and then in
the subparagraphs which go over the page.
It's very clear, just looking at what those issues
are, in terms of the representations made.
Starting at bundle {D1-9}, subparagraph 16.1.1:
"The claimant's capital would be protected and they
would not lose money ..."
In bundle {F1-5}:
"There was only a negligible chance the claimant's
capital would fail to appreciate ..."
HIS HONOUR:  Yes.
MR JONES:  These are all pre-contractual representations.
They are very much focused at the early stage.
If one turns to the list of issues by the parties,
one can see at {B3-19}, and then forward to page 10, for
example, in relation to the misrepresentation claim,
they are all focused on, again, pre-contractual
representations which have been relied on in the
re-amended particulars of claim.
I think my learned friend took you to those at
Unless you would like me to, I don't propose to take
you back to the claimant's re-amended particulars of
claim.
HIS HONOUR:  It's the protection point.
MR JONES:  Protection, exactly.  It's all about what was
said to induce the claimant to enter into these
products.
Again, I'll develop this further, but this is the
only focus of attention in terms of agency at that
point -- again, subject to what happens.
If I could open {C1-5}.
HIS HONOUR:  {C1-5}, yes, I'm up to date with that.
MR JONES:  Perfect.
Bundle {E2} should now be {E1} -- well, it's
19 pages on the PDF, but the last page is 25, and that's
been updated very recently.
I don't know if your Lordship has that last --
HIS HONOUR:  No.  What's come in recently in bundle {E4}?
MR JONES:  Certainly I received it this morning.  There is
a clip of about 8 or 12 pages, an email exchange and
a letter from the claimant a couple of days ago.
It sounds like Mr David is with us.
MR DAVID:  Hold on one second.  I'm on my telephone with the
technical support.
They say, first of all, I have to get online on my
telephone, and then they will do some magic to ensure
that I get on on my laptop.
So just for the technical support chap, do I now
come off the link on my telephone?
(Pause).
MR JONES:  I don't know if it would be convenient to finish
off the housekeeping.  I don't think Mr David will
accuse me of leaving him out.
HIS HONOUR:  Yes.
MR JONES:  So the final page of bundle {E5} is numbered 95.
